**Section:** Cariyāpiṭaka (cp)

**Title (Pali):** Mahāsudassanacariya

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāsudassanacariya* ("The Conduct of Mahāsudassana", Cp 4 or I.4) is the fourth poetic narrative in the Pali *Cariyāpiṭaka* [Bareau; Matsumura 1980; SuttaCentral]. Like the other poems in the collection, it presents an abridged poetic treatment of a well-known past life of the Bodhisatta [Bareau]. The narrative of King Mahāsudassana forms part of a wider narrative tradition attested elsewhere in the Pali canon, notably in the *Mahāsudassana-sutta* (DN 17), and in northern Buddhist literature, including Sanskrit witnesses from the Turfan manuscripts [Matsumura 1980]. The canonical poem is commented upon in Dhammapāla's *Paramatthadīpanī* (*Cariyā-Piṭakaṭṭhakathā*) [Matsumura 1980]. Modern translations include an English version by Bhikkhu Sujato as well as French and other translations [Bareau; SuttaCentral].

According to DharmaNexus text-reuse data, the *Mahāsudassanacariya* shares three passages with the seventh volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, with its longest shared match occurring between segments §2.4–4.4 and §2150–2154 [DharmaNexus]. The text is also noted on SuttaCentral in connection with the *Mahānāradakassapajātaka* (Ja 545) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus additionally records six automatic cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā* (D3790), though these represent machine-detected formulaic reuses rather than direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
